statement: A motion-sensor floodlight detects movement up to $18$ feet away, across an angle of $150^\circ$, so the region it covers is a sector of a circle. What is the area, in square feet, of that region?

choices.misconception: I found the length of the curved edge of the sector, 150 over 360 times 36 pi = 15 pi, instead of its area.
I used 180 degrees as the full circle, so I took 150 over 180 of 324 pi and got 270 pi.
I treated 18 feet as the diameter of the circle, so I used a radius of 9 and took 5/12 of 81 pi, which is 33.75 pi.

hints: The covered region is a fraction of a full circle of radius $18$. What fraction?
A $150^\circ$ sector is $\frac{150}{360} = \frac{5}{12}$ of the whole circle. Multiply that fraction by the area of the full circle.
The full circle has area $\pi(18)^2 = 324\pi$, so the sector has area $\frac{5}{12} \cdot 324\pi$.

solutions.reliable: The light covers a sector with radius $18$ feet and central angle $150^\circ$. The full circle has area $\pi \cdot 18^2 = 324\pi$, and the sector is $\frac{150}{360} = \frac{5}{12}$ of it. So the area is $\frac{5}{12} \cdot 324\pi = 135\pi$ square feet, about $424$ square feet.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
